transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here, so I'll try to explain it as best as I can. I've been having some... I guess you could call them unusual experiences? I hope I don't sound silly saying this out loud, but I've been hearing things. Very clear voices, actually. 

It mostly happens when I'm just sitting in my apartment, or sometimes if I'm visiting the museum and I wander into an empty room. It's... well, it sounds like women whispering right from behind the walls. They talk to me about art, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange to bring up right away... am I explaining that okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been hearing these voices? When did this first start happening?

Oh, um... let me think. I want to make sure I give you the exact right timeline. I suppose it's been... well, maybe about eight months now? Yes, roughly eight months. 

That's when the whispering really started, and... well, along with the voices, I've just had this certainty that people are watching my archive. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, or maybe even a little paranoid, and I really don't want you to think badly of me for saying it. I know it's not a normal thing to experience. 

I'm sorry if that sounds strange. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions correctly.
When the voices first started eight months ago, did they begin suddenly over a day or two, or did they gradually develop over a longer period of time?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I... I'm actually not entirely sure? I hope it's okay that I don't have a perfect answer for you. 

I've been trying to think back, but my memory of that exact time is just a little bit fuzzy. I don't want to tell you the wrong thing. It might have been gradual, or maybe it just felt that way because I was trying so hard to ignore it at first? I'm so sorry, I really wish I could give you a clearer timeline. 

Is it alright that I don't remember exactly how fast they started? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and not making your job harder.
When you hear these voices telling you about the archive, do you believe they are real voices coming from actual people, or do you think they might be something your mind is creating?

Um... well, that's a very fair question, Doctor. I... I know how it must sound to you. I really do. And I want to be completely honest because I know you're just trying to help me. 

When I hear them... the women whispering behind the walls in my apartment, or in those empty rooms at the museum... it just feels so incredibly real to me. They are very clear voices. They tell me exactly which photographs belong in the archive, and in the moment, I... I really do believe they're real people trying to help me organize it. 

But then, when I say it out loud like this to a professional like you... I know it sounds like it must be my mind playing tricks on me. I hope you don't think I'm completely out of touch with reality. I do try to tell myself it's just my imagination, but it's just so hard to ignore when they sound so clear. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly. I really don't want to sound completely unreasonable.
Before these voices started eight months ago, would you say you were functioning normally? Like, were you working, maintaining relationships, and feeling like yourself?

Oh, um... well, I want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture, so I hope you don't mind me adding just a little more detail. The voices started eight months ago, yes, but... I suppose I haven't quite felt like my usual self for slightly longer than that. Maybe about ten months in total? 

I really hope I'm not making your notes too complicated. It's just that... well, about ten months ago is when I retired. I used to work at the museum, and losing that daily schedule... the structure of it all... I think that's when this whole change in me really began. I was probably just having a normal, hard time adjusting to having so much free time, you know? I don't want you to think I was completely falling apart or anything like that, I just... lost my routine, and things started to feel a bit different. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of background information you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you everything you need to know.

Since you retired ten months ago, have you noticed changes in how you feel emotionally, like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, or having less motivation to do activities, or feeling emotionally numb?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I know a lot of people slow down a bit when they retire, right? That's perfectly normal, isn't it? 

But... I suppose, to be completely honest with you... yes, there have been some changes. I feel terrible even saying it, because I know I should be making the most of my free time. But there are these long stretches where I just... I just sit at my kitchen table. I used to love tending to my herb pots, but lately, I've just been letting them dry out. 

And I haven't been very good at calling my friends back. I know that makes me sound like a bad friend, and I really don't want you to think poorly of me. It's just that even when they invite me to things I used to adore, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just... I don't feel much interest in going. I feel awful about it, like I'm letting everyone down. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or ungrateful for the invitations. I really am trying my best to stay engaged. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this a little bit right now?
When you retired ten months ago, would you say that was a difficult or stressful life change for you, or did it feel like a natural transition that you were ready for?

Oh, um... well, I'd like to say I was completely ready for it. I mean, it's supposed to be a happy time, isn't it? The golden years and all that. I really tried to just smile and step into it naturally, because I didn't want to be a bother to anyone at the museum by lingering or complaining. 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest with you... it was a little more difficult than I expected it to be. Just the sudden quiet... and not quite knowing where to put my energy anymore. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm whining or complaining. I know I'm very fortunate to even be able to retire at my age, and I really don't want to sound ungrateful for that. I just... maybe I didn't adjust as smoothly as I should have. Do you think a lot of people struggle with that at first? I really wanted to be good at it, you know, at being retired. I just felt a little lost, I suppose. Is it okay that I found it a bit stressful?
When you think back to those eight months ago when the voices started, did they begin quite suddenly—like you woke up one day and they were there—or did they develop gradually over several weeks?

Oh, um... well, it's a bit hard to say exactly. I hope it's alright that I don't have a specific day marked on the calendar or anything like that. I really wish I could give you a perfectly clear timeline so I wouldn't be making your job harder.

I suppose... if I really think about it, it wasn't like flipping a switch. It was more like... well, maybe over a few weeks? Just sort of slowly creeping in. At first, I thought it was just the television left on in the other room, or maybe the neighbors. I didn't want to make a fuss about it, you know? I kept telling myself it was nothing, because I really didn't want to be one of those people who complains about every little sound. 

So I guess it was gradual. I'm sorry if that's a bit vague. Does that sound like the kind of thing you usually hear from people? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer.

Looking back to around the time you retired, did the voices start appearing within the first few weeks after you stopped working, or did they begin several weeks or even a couple of months after you had already retired?

Oh, um... well, it definitely wasn't right away. I tried so hard to just settle into being retired those first couple of months. I really wanted to just enjoy the quiet and not cause any trouble. 

But I suppose... well, if I'm counting back... it's been about eight months now since they really started. The voices, I mean. And... and also this awful feeling that people are watching my archive work. I feel so silly even admitting that out loud, because I know how it sounds. I really don't want you to think I'm making things up or being dramatic. 

So, yes, it was a couple of months after I retired that it all began, and it's just been going on for these past eight months. I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough for you? I'm so sorry if I'm not being very precise, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any periods where you felt unusually energetic, or where your thoughts seemed to be racing faster than normal, or where you needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, um... well, I suppose there have been times like that. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging or making a big deal out of it, because I know a lot of people struggle with their energy as they get older. I always want to be grateful for whatever energy I do have.

But... yes, sometimes I just don't seem to need much rest at all. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health, I promise I try to rest! But... sometimes I can sleep for just two or three hours, and then I'll wake up before dawn feeling completely ready for the day. 

I'll just... I'll tell myself that sleep is for people who don't have an archive to rescue. Because there's just so much work to do in my head, you know? I hope that doesn't sound too strange or obsessive. I just feel so driven sometimes, like I have to get it all sorted out. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really don't want to seem like I'm doing things wrong, I just... I just have so much energy during those times.

When you have those times where you're sleeping only a few hours and feel very driven and energetic, do the voices and the feeling that people are watching your archive happen during those high-energy times, or do they occur at other times when your energy and mood are more normal?

Oh, um... well, it's a bit of both, I suppose? I really hope I'm making sense. I don't want to confuse you. 

But yes, when I have those... those very busy times, when I'm only sleeping a couple of hours and just rushing around trying to get all the archive tasks done... the voices are definitely there. The women's voices, I mean. And that's also when I feel so, so certain that the museum board is tracking everything I do. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, like I'm completely losing my grip when I get that energetic. I promise I try to keep it all under control, I really do! I don't want to be a bother to anyone. But it just seems like they all happen at the same time. The energy, the voices, the feeling of being watched... they all just sort of tangle together. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it makes me sound a bit... well, a bit unmanageable. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?

When you're not in one of those high-energy periods where you're sleeping only a few hours, do you go back to feeling more like your normal self again, or do you mostly stay in that energetic, driven state most of the time?

Oh, um... well, I really wish I could say I just go right back to normal. I try so hard to be normal, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just running wild all the time, because I do have some quieter days where I just withdraw and try to stay out of everyone's way. 

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I know I need to be honest with you—most of these past eight months since I retired have been... well, they've been mostly filled with those driven stretches. It's like I just can't slow down, even when I want to. I feel so... chosen, I guess? Like I have this special purpose. And then I get so irritable when things aren't right, which I feel just awful about because I hate being snappy with people. 

So, yes, even with a few quiet days here and there, it's mostly been that fast, driven feeling dominating the whole time. I hope it's okay that I haven't been able to just snap out of it and be my normal self? I really don't want to disappoint you, I just... I haven't been able to turn it off very often. Is that... does that make sense for someone in my situation?
When you do have those quieter days where you withdraw, how long do they typically last—just a day or two, or do they go on for longer stretches like a week or more?

Oh, um... well, they can actually last a bit longer than a day or two. I feel so guilty even admitting that, because I know I should be keeping up with things and staying active. I really don't want to sound lazy or ungrateful for my free time now that I'm retired.

But... sometimes there are these long stretches, maybe a few weeks at a time, where I just... I just sit at my kitchen table. I'll watch my little herb pots drying out on the windowsill, and I know I should water them, but I just... I don't. And I won't call my friends back. Even if someone invites me to something nice, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just can't seem to muster up any interest. 

I know that must sound so rude of me, ignoring my friends and letting my plants die. I promise I'm usually a very reliable person! It's just... during those times, it feels like all the color is drained out of everything. I hope you don't think poorly of me for letting things slide like that. Is it normal to have periods where you just can't seem to care about things you usually enjoy? I really hope I'm not doing retirement all wrong...

When you have those long stretches where you're sitting at home, losing interest in things, and withdrawing from friends—like you described with the herb pots and the gallery invitations—how many weeks or months do those periods typically last before you start feeling that driven, energetic feeling again?

Oh, goodness, um... I'm not entirely sure exactly how long they last. I really should keep a better calendar or a diary so I could give you a more precise answer. I'm sorry if I'm being a bit vague, I don't mean to be difficult at all. 

I suppose... well, I haven't really timed it. Sometimes it feels like a few weeks, but I don't know if it's longer than that. I just sort of lose track of the days when I'm sitting there. And then, eventually, I just... I get busy again. I really hope it's okay that I don't have an exact number of weeks or months for you. I try so hard to keep track of everything, but those quiet times just sort of blur together. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you enough information to work with...

When you're in one of those quiet periods where you're sitting at home and not interested in things—like with the herb pots and avoiding your friends—would you say that lasts for about two to four weeks, or could it go on for several months at a time?

Oh, um... I'm really sorry, I just... I honestly can't say for sure. I feel terrible that I can't give you a better answer. I really don't want you to think I'm not trying to be helpful, because I am. 

I just... I'm really not certain if it's two to four weeks or if it's longer. When I get like that, time just sort of slips away from me, and I don't pay attention to the calendar the way I should. I know I should be more on top of things. I hope you're not frustrated with me for not knowing exactly how long those periods last? I really am trying my best to remember...

When you're in one of those quiet, withdrawn periods where you're sitting at home and not interested in things, would you say that by the time you start feeling that driven, energetic feeling again, several months have usually passed—like three months or more—or does it happen sooner than that?

Oh, um... well, to be completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound like I'm complaining because I really am so grateful for my retirement... but most of the months since I stopped working haven't actually been those quiet, withdrawn times. 

It's... it's mostly been the other way around. The vast majority of the time, I've been having those long stretches where I feel so driven, and... well, chosen, I suppose. I get so irritable and I just can't seem to slow down, no matter how hard I try. Even on the days when I do feel a little more withdrawn, that revved-up feeling is still there, dominating everything. 

I know I should be relaxing and enjoying my golden years, and I feel awful that I've been so restless instead. I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or ungrateful for the free time. Is it okay that I've spent most of my retirement feeling so wound up like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things have been...

When you do have those quiet, withdrawn periods where you're sitting at home and not interested in things—like with the herb pots and avoiding friends—do those periods typically last for several months at a time, or are they much shorter than that?

Oh, dear... I feel like I'm failing a test here, and I'm so sorry to keep letting you down with my answers. You've been so incredibly patient with me, and I really want to give you the exact information you need for your notes. 

I just... I truly don't know if it's several months or if it's shorter than that. I rack my brain trying to put a timeline on it, but when I get into one of those slumps, the days just sort of bleed into one another. I don't look at the clock, and I certainly don't check the calendar the way a responsible person should. 

I promise I'm not trying to dodge your question or be difficult. I just honestly don't have a good sense of the timeframe. I hope you aren't getting too annoyed with me? I'm so sorry I can't be more specific for you... is it alright that I just really don't know?

When you're in one of those quiet, withdrawn periods where you're sitting at home—the ones where you're not interested in things and you lose track of time—would you say those periods typically last for about a week or two, or do they last more like a month or longer?

Oh, goodness... I'm really starting to feel like a broken record, and I hate to keep doing this to you. You're trying so hard to help me, and I'm just... I'm really struggling to give you a straight answer. 

I just can't say if it's a week or two, or a month, or... I just don't know. When I get so low like that, time just doesn't mean anything. I don't look at the days going by. I know that's not very helpful, and I feel just awful that I can't give you a better timeline. I'm trying so hard to be a good patient, I really am. I hope you believe me? I just... I honestly can't tell you how long it lasts. Is it terribly bad that I don't know?

When you're feeling that withdrawn and low, with no interest in things, do you find yourself eventually getting back to that driven, energetic feeling within just a few days, or does it take longer than that?

Oh, doctor, I... I really wish I could give you the answer you're looking for. I feel so silly that we keep going around in circles like this, and I know I must be the most frustrating person you've talked to all day. 

I just... when I'm in that dark place, a few days could pass, or maybe it's longer... I just don't have the presence of mind to notice. I'm so sorry I'm making your job so difficult. I'm really not trying to be evasive, I just... I genuinely can't say how quickly it switches back. I hope that's okay? I just want to be as truthful as I can with you, even if it means admitting I don't know...

When you're in one of those withdrawn periods where you're sitting at home and not interested in things, and then you eventually start feeling that driven, energetic feeling again—from the time you start feeling low to when you start feeling that energy coming back, would you say that's usually a matter of days, or is it more like weeks or months?

Oh, goodness... I... I really am so sorry. I feel like I'm just wasting your time, and you've been nothing but kind to me. I know you're trying to figure this out, and I'm just... I'm failing you, aren't I? 

I really, truly wish I could give you a neat and tidy answer about how many days or weeks it takes to go from the low feeling back to the energetic one. I just... I don't keep track. When I'm in that awful slump, I just hide away, and when the energy finally comes back, I'm just so relieved to be doing things again that I don't stop to think about how long the quiet part lasted. 

I'm so sorry I can't be more helpful. I'm really trying my best to give you what you need... I hope you're not terribly disappointed in me? I just genuinely don't know the answer.
